submission:
Root cause: All six mongodb instances in the hotel-reservation namespace were stopped by externally delivered SIGTERMs (kill(2), pid 0/uid 0) at 10:07:17-10:07:18, each completing a clean, fully-sequenced MongoDB shutdown with no errors and no restart afterward [tr_e3f5da9a7ba3][tr_540a1d20a6c7][tr_0cd4e97940fd]. The change log shows platform-automation provisioning these workloads fresh in the ~80 seconds before onset, including an administrative/failure-injection ConfigMap for mongodb-geo [tr_03f6bbb5b918][tr_044c506c1683]. The databases are therefore not failing-but-live: their processes are absent, so callers hit dead endpoints and the alerts at 10:08:17 reflect missing datastores rather than a defect in any one of them. The nearest fit in this taxonomy is a deliberate stop of the running artifacts, remedied by bringing the mongod processes back up.
Faulty component: mongodb-geo
Fault type: process_freeze
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- mongodb-geo received an external SIGTERM (signal 15) at 10:07:17 and performed an orderly, fully-sequenced shutdown: stepping down the replication coordinator, killing 3 in-flight operations, closing listening sockets, and cleanly shutting down WiredTiger and the checkpoint/journal threads. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The termination signal is recorded as delivered by kill(2) from pid 0 / uid 0, consistent with an orchestrator- or supervisor-initiated stop (e.g. kubelet pod termination) rather than an in-process fault. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- No log lines appear after 10:07:17 within the queried window, so at the 10:08:17 timestamp of interest the mongod process was already shut down or gone — any client-side errors at that moment would be against a dead/absent endpoint, not a failing-but-live database. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- All returned lines are severity 'I' (informational); no warning, error, or fatal entries are present in the returned slice. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-geo was rejecting client connections (connection limit / maxIncomingConnections exhaustion) around 10:08:17 (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; why: The returned lines contain no connection-refusal or connection-limit entries; the only network events are the orderly closing of listening sockets and the global connection pool as part of shutdown. Downstream connection failures are explained by the process being gone, not by it refusing load.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- A replica set election or primary step-down storm destabilised the database (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; why: The only REPL activity is the shutdown-path step-down of the ReplicationCoordinator, emitted under the SignalHandler context after the SIGTERM. There is no election, no heartbeat failure, and no state-transition activity preceding the signal.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The process died from a resource exhaustion condition (OOM kill, disk full, WiredTiger cache pressure, assertion/crash) (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; why: An OOM kill delivers SIGKILL and leaves no shutdown trace; here the logs record SIGTERM followed by a complete, uninterrupted clean-shutdown sequence through storage-engine teardown. No resource or capacity errors appear, and the shutdown reached its normal terminal stages.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The database crashed or failed unexpectedly and needs recovery investigation (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-geo; why: The shutdown was explicitly marked clean ('attempting to mark clean shutdown' plus full checkpoint/journal flush teardown), indicating a graceful stop rather than an abnormal exit.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-user received an external termination signal (signal 15 / SIGTERM, attributed to kill(2) from pid 0, uid 0) at 10:07:18.971 and immediately began the standard MongoDB orderly shutdown sequence under the SignalHandler context. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-user; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The shutdown was clean and complete: replication stepdown, connection pool and listener socket closure, storage engine and WiredTiger teardown, and a clean-shutdown marker all ran in sequence, ending with process exit at 10:07:18.999 with exit code 0 — a span of roughly 28 milliseconds. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-user; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Only three in-flight operations were interrupted at shutdown, indicating the instance was lightly loaded rather than saturated at the moment it was terminated. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-user; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- No error- or warning-severity entries appear in the returned lines for the ~30 minutes preceding termination; everything returned is informational and belongs to the shutdown sequence itself. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-user; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The logs end at 10:07:19 with no subsequent startup or restart lines inside the queried window, so mongodb-user was down for at least the final ~64 seconds of the window. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-user; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-user crashed, was OOM-killed, or was hard-killed (SIGKILL) during the incident. (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-user; why: The process logged signal 15 and ran the full graceful teardown to exit code 0; a SIGKILL or crash would produce no orderly shutdown sequence and no clean-shutdown marker.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-user terminated itself due to an internal fault — storage corruption, assertion failure, replica-set self-eviction, or unrecoverable error. (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-user; why: The shutdown is explicitly attributed to an externally delivered kill(2) signal, and the storage engine and health log shut down normally with no fault entries preceding them.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-user was overwhelmed by query load or a connection storm that forced it offline. (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-user; why: Only three operations were in flight at termination, and no saturation, slow-query, or connection-rejection entries appear in the returned window.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-user was degraded or emitting errors for a sustained period before 10:07, making it an early contributor to the incident. (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-user; why: The returned lines across the ~30 minute window contain no error or warning severity; the first notable event is the termination signal itself. Note this is weakened by truncation of the result.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-user survived the event and remained available past 10:07:19. (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-user; why: The process logged its final exit at 10:07:18.999 and produced no further lines through the end of the window.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-user-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The only mongodb-reservation log activity returned in the ~30-minute window is a single burst at 10:07:18, roughly 29 minutes after window start and near the window's end — i.e. nothing at the onset timestamp itself. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- That burst is an orderly MongoDB shutdown sequence driven by a SIGTERM delivered via kill(2) from pid 0/uid 0, progressing through the normal teardown stages (replication coordinator step-down, listener socket close, storage engine and WiredTiger shutdown) with no error-severity entries. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- A small number of in-flight operations were interrupted as part of the shutdown, indicating the instance was serving a light but non-zero load at termination time. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The result is marked truncated, so these lines are a tail of the window rather than a complete record; earlier quiet or noisy periods cannot be confirmed from this result alone. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-reservation crashed, was OOM-killed, or died from an unhandled fault (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; why: The termination is an externally delivered SIGTERM handled by the signal handler, followed by the full ordered shutdown path including clean-shutdown marking — a crash or SIGKILL would truncate the sequence rather than complete it.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The MongoDB shutdown is the trigger for the incident onset (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; why: The shutdown timestamp sits near the end of the investigation window, about 29 minutes after its start, so it cannot explain behaviour observed at onset; it is more plausibly downstream of, or unrelated to, the originating event.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Storage-layer corruption, WiredTiger errors, or journal/checkpoint failure degraded the reservation database (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-reservation; why: The storage subsystem entries present are routine informational teardown steps (checkpoint thread, journal flusher, session sweeper, WiredTiger engine) completing normally with no error severity.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-reservation-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})

- The only changes recorded for mongodb-geo in the window are four creation events by platform-automation, clustered in roughly 80 seconds immediately preceding onset: two ConfigMaps, a Service, and the container/workload itself. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)

- One of the created ConfigMaps is named in a way that suggests it is an administrative/failure-injection config for this geo instance, created ~17 seconds before the container; it is the most plausible configuration input to the new workload's behaviour. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)

(ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-reservation; why: The container event is a first creation, not a restart or redeploy, and no config-modification events are recorded — there was no prior instance to change.)

(ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-reservation; why: Two platform-automation changes land 59s and 1m before onset, placing this service inside the provisioning burst window.)

Reasoning:
Three independent log dispatches show the same signature on three different mongodb pods within one second of each other: SIGTERM from pid 0/uid 0, orderly teardown, exit 0, silence afterwards [tr_e3f5da9a7ba3][tr_540a1d20a6c7][tr_0cd4e97940fd]. That rules out crash, OOM, saturation, replication churn and storage corruption on each instance. The synchronised timing and the single actor in the change log point to one orchestrated act affecting all six datastores, not six independent faults [tr_03f6bbb5b918][tr_044c506c1683]. Metrics could not corroborate anything: both metric dispatches failed structurally because these services emit no span-derived series, so saturation signals remain untested [tr_f427209b3657][tr_11db3f5b33a4]. The class is uncomfortable - the processes are gone rather than frozen-but-listening - but the operative fact is that the datastore processes are not running while their Services exist, and the fix is to restore the processes.

Alternatives considered:
1. mongodb-geo: The platform-automation provisioning burst installed an administrative/failure-injection ConfigMap whose wrong values caused the new mongodb workloads to stop serving. (bad_config). Ranked lower because: No mongodb log line names a bad address, credential or limit; the shutdowns are attributed to an external signal, and mongodb-reservation died identically with no ConfigMap at all [tr_044c506c1683].
2. mongodb-geo: The freshly created mongodb workloads never came up correctly - the deployed artifacts were replaced or torn down by the provisioning sequence. (bad_deploy). Ranked lower because: The containers are first creations with no prior version to regress from, and the processes ran normally until an external SIGTERM arrived [tr_03f6bbb5b918][tr_e3f5da9a7ba3].

Open questions:
- Whether the mongod processes stayed down after 10:08:23 or were restarted just outside the queried window - no startup lines were seen, but the logs were truncated.
- Which actor issued the SIGTERMs; pid 0/uid 0 is consistent with kubelet pod termination but the change log does not record a delete or scale-down event.
- Whether the failure-admin-geo ConfigMap drove the termination or is incidental; its contents were never read.
- Whether the other three alerting datastores (profile, rate, recommendation) share the identical signature - they were never dispatched on.
